I changed `spec/rails_helper.rb` so leftover rows from `before(:all)` are reported and removed. I only ran `spec/models/admissions/letter_request_spec.rb` alone, and it passes (6 examples, 0 failures). I did not run the bisect pair from the issue or the full suite.

My run showed no "Leaked objects" warning, even though the issue says the spec leaves a record behind. I only looked at the tail of the output, so the warning may have scrolled off. I did not confirm that the check fires or that it clears that record.

I added a `LeakDetector` module with two parts:
- **Full model list:** it calls `Rails.application.eager_load!` before scanning, so it sees every model locally and not only in CI. It skips abstract classes and models whose table doesn't exist.
- **Check after every spec group:** a new `config.after(:all)` hook runs the check when each context ends, and the existing `after(:suite)` hook runs it once more. This catches leaks that are cleaned up before the suite ends. When it finds rows, it prints which models leaked and truncates all tables.

I did not edit `letter_request_spec.rb`. Its `after(:all)` still deletes only two of the three records, and the new hook now cleans up the third (the `AdmissionProcess`). The spec's own cleanup is still incomplete.

The hook runs after every group, not only top-level ones, so it does a count query per model each time. That adds some runtime across the 2253 examples. I have not measured it.
